quests.instruction: A weather app uses little pictures instead of words.
quests.question: Which picture would show a snowy day?
options: A cloud with slanted lines beneath it
A cloud with white flakes beneath it
A Sun with rays all around
A cloud with a zigzag bolt
quests.correctAnswer: A cloud with white flakes beneath it
quests.hint: Imagine what falls on a snowy day and how you'd draw it.
quests.explanation: Snow is drawn as flakes under a cloud. Slanted lines are rain, rays are sunshine and a bolt is lightning.
quests.funFact: Weather symbols let people who speak different languages read the same forecast.

quests.instruction: Hari's forecast shows a Sun that is half-hidden behind a small cloud.
quests.question: What does this symbol mean?
quests.hint: Notice how much of each picture shows.
quests.explanation: A Sun peeking out from a cloud shows both sunshine and cloud, so the sky is mixed.
quests.funFact: A symbol like this is often used when the Sun will be in and out all day.

quests.instruction: On a wind map, small arrows point from left to right across the screen.
quests.question: What could the arrows show?
options: Which way the wind is blowing
How deep the rain will be
quests.correctAnswer: Which way the wind is blowing
quests.hint: Arrows usually show movement.
quests.explanation: Arrows on a wind map show the direction the wind is moving, and sometimes their length shows speed.
quests.funFact: Many weather maps use arrows or little barbs to show wind direction and speed.

quests.instruction: A forecast for four days says Monday 22°C, Tuesday 27°C, Wednesday 19°C and Thursday 25°C.
quests.question: On which day would a light jacket be most useful?
quests.hint: Find the coolest day.
quests.explanation: Wednesday has the lowest temperature at 19°C, so a light jacket would be most useful.
quests.funFact: A forecast's daily high usually happens in the afternoon.

quests.instruction: Tomorrow's forecast says: high 29°C, low 18°C.
quests.question: What is the difference between the high and the low?
quests.hint: Subtract the lower number from the higher one.
quests.explanation: Twenty-nine minus eighteen is eleven, so the temperature will swing by 11 degrees.
quests.funFact: Clear, dry days often have a bigger gap between the high and the low.

quests.instruction: Daily temperatures were Monday 24°C, Tuesday 26°C, Wednesday 18°C, Thursday 17°C and Friday 20°C.
quests.question: Between which two days was the biggest drop?
quests.hint: Look for the largest fall, not the lowest number.
quests.explanation: From 26°C to 18°C is a drop of 8 degrees, which is bigger than any other change.
quests.funFact: A sudden drop in temperature often happens when a cold front passes.

quests.instruction: The forecast says there is a 10% chance of rain this afternoon.
quests.question: How should Ana read this?
options: It will rain on 10% of the town
Rain is expected but will be light
It will rain for 10% of the afternoon
quests.hint: Think of 10 out of 100 chances.
quests.explanation: A 10% chance means it will probably stay dry, though a shower can't be completely ruled out.
quests.funFact: Forecasters base rain chances on how often rain fell in similar conditions.

quests.instruction: The chances of rain this week are Monday 20%, Tuesday 70%, Wednesday 40% and Thursday 5%.
quests.question: On which day is an umbrella the best idea?
quests.hint: Higher percentages mean rain is more likely.
quests.explanation: Seventy percent is the highest chance of rain, so Tuesday is the day to carry an umbrella.
quests.funFact: Even a very low rain chance doesn't completely rule out a shower.

quests.instruction: One forecast says 'showers' and another says 'steady rain'.
quests.question: What is the difference?
options: Steady rain is lighter than showers
Showers are made of snow, not of rain
Showers come and go; steady rain stays
quests.correctAnswer: Showers come and go; steady rain stays
quests.hint: Consider whether the rain comes and goes.
quests.explanation: A shower comes and goes, often with dry spells between. Steady rain falls for hours without a break.
quests.funFact: A single shower often comes from one cloud passing overhead.

quests.instruction: The forecast says: wind 15 km/h from the east.
quests.question: What does this mean?
options: There will be 15 mm of wind
Air is moving from west to east at 15 km/h
Air is moving from east to west at 15 km/h
quests.correctAnswer: Air is moving from east to west at 15 km/h
quests.hint: Winds are named for where they start.
quests.explanation: A wind from the east starts in the east and blows toward the west.
quests.funFact: Forecast gust speeds are higher than average speeds because wind comes in bursts.

quests.instruction: The forecast says: wind 20 km/h with gusts up to 55 km/h.
quests.question: What are gusts?
quests.hint: Ask yourself whether the wind stays the same.
quests.explanation: Gusts are quick, stronger bursts that come and go on top of the steady wind.
quests.funFact: Gusts can be much stronger than the average wind speed.

quests.instruction: On this wind map, longer arrows mean faster wind. Over the coast the arrows are long; inland they are short.
quests.question: What does the map show?
options: Wind is stronger on the coast
It is raining on the coast
quests.correctAnswer: Wind is stronger on the coast
quests.hint: Compare the arrow lengths with the rule on the map.
quests.explanation: Long arrows show strong wind, so the coast is windier than inland.
quests.funFact: Wind is often stronger near coasts because there are fewer obstacles over water.

quests.instruction: A bar chart shows rainfall: Monday 2 mm, Tuesday 6 mm, Wednesday 0 mm, Thursday 4 mm.
quests.question: How many days had more than 3 mm of rain?
quests.hint: Only count the bars taller than 3.
quests.explanation: Tuesday with 6 mm and Thursday with 4 mm are the only days above 3 mm.
quests.funFact: Bar charts make it easy to compare amounts at a glance.

quests.instruction: A temperature line on a chart climbs from 6 am, peaks, then falls toward the evening.
quests.question: When is the warmest time of day likely to be?
quests.hint: Find the highest point of the line.
quests.explanation: The line peaks in the early afternoon, when the ground has had hours of sunshine.
quests.funFact: The warmest time comes after noon because the heated ground keeps warming the air.

quests.instruction: A picture chart uses one umbrella icon for every 2 rainy days. April has four umbrella icons.
quests.question: How many rainy days did April have?
quests.hint: Each icon stands for more than one day.
quests.explanation: Four icons times two days each makes eight rainy days.
quests.funFact: Picture charts, called pictograms, use symbols to stand for numbers.

quests.instruction: The forecast says: bright sunshine in the morning, showers in the afternoon. The class can go to the park for one hour.
quests.question: When should they go?
quests.hint: Match the outing to the dry part of the day.
quests.explanation: The morning will be sunny, so that is the best time to be outdoors.
quests.funFact: Many forecasts split the day into morning, afternoon and evening.

quests.instruction: The overnight low is forecast to be 1°C, and Dad has some delicate plants in pots outside.
quests.question: What is a sensible step?
options: Give them extra water at midnight
Cover them or bring them indoors
quests.correctAnswer: Cover them or bring them indoors
quests.hint: Imagine how plants cope with cold nights.
quests.explanation: Cold air near freezing can harm delicate plants, so covering or moving them protects them.
quests.funFact: Frost can form even when the forecast low is a few degrees above zero.

quests.instruction: Sunset is at 6:05 pm. Tara wants her evening walk to end before dark.
quests.question: When should she start?
quests.hint: Dark begins after sunset.
quests.explanation: Starting at 5 pm leaves about an hour before the Sun goes down.
quests.funFact: The sky stays light for a while after sunset, a time called twilight.

quests.instruction: City A and City B both have a temperature of 18°C. City A is sunny and City B is rainy.
quests.question: How will the two cities compare for someone walking outside?
options: They will feel the same to everyone
City B must be the warmer of the two
City A must have the heavier rain
quests.hint: Focus on how sun and rain change how warm you feel.
quests.explanation: Sun and rain change how warm or cool it feels even at the same temperature.
quests.funFact: Rain and wind change how we feel the temperature.

quests.instruction: A weather app shows 31°C but a 'feels like' temperature of 35°C.
quests.question: Why might it feel hotter than the thermometer says?
options: A cold wind is blowing across the town
The thick clouds are trapping the heat
Humid air makes sweating less effective
quests.correctAnswer: Humid air makes sweating less effective
quests.hint: Remember how muggy air feels.
quests.explanation: Humid air slows the drying of sweat, so your body can't cool as well, and it feels hotter.
quests.funFact: The 'heat index' combines temperature and humidity to show how hot it feels.

quests.instruction: The forecast shows a UV index of 9, which is labelled very high.
quests.question: What should you do outside?
options: Put on a heavy coat to stay safe
Wear sunscreen and a hat, and find shade
Ignore it, because the day is cool
Stay inside a dark room for the whole day
quests.correctAnswer: Wear sunscreen and a hat, and find shade
quests.hint: UV is about the Sun's rays, not the temperature.
quests.explanation: A high UV index means skin can burn quickly, so protect it with sunscreen, a hat and shade.
quests.funFact: UV can be strong even on a cool day.

quests.instruction: On a rain radar loop, a green patch is moving steadily from the west toward town.
quests.question: What does the radar suggest?
options: The rain has already passed the town
Snow is just about to begin
Rain will probably reach town soon
quests.correctAnswer: Rain will probably reach town soon
quests.hint: Which direction is the patch heading?
quests.explanation: Radar shows where rain is and how it is moving. A patch coming toward town means rain is on the way.
quests.funFact: Radar pictures are updated every few minutes.

quests.instruction: A satellite picture of the country shows large white swirling patches.
quests.question: What do the white patches show?
quests.hint: Satellites look down from space at the sky.
quests.explanation: From space, clouds look white and swirly, so satellite photos help forecasters see where they are.
quests.funFact: Weather satellites take pictures of clouds many times a day.

quests.instruction: A weather map shows a large letter L over the area where Dev lives. L stands for low pressure.
quests.question: Which weather is more common under a low?
quests.hint: Remember what falling air pressure often means.
quests.explanation: Low pressure tends to bring clouds and rain, while high pressure tends to bring settled, dry weather.
quests.funFact: Winds spiral around areas of high and low pressure.

quests.instruction: At 5 pm the temperature is 20°C and it is falling by 2°C every hour.
quests.question: What will it be at 8 pm?
quests.hint: Count three hours, subtracting two each time.
quests.explanation: After three hours, it falls by 6 degrees, from 20°C to 14°C.
quests.funFact: Evening temperatures fall fastest soon after sunset.

quests.instruction: A table shows rain in mm for four weeks: week 1 had 12, week 2 had 0, week 3 had 25 and week 4 had 9.
quests.question: What was the total rainfall?
quests.hint: Add all four weeks together.
quests.explanation: Twelve plus zero plus twenty-five plus nine equals 46 millimetres.
quests.funFact: Monthly rainfall totals help gardeners and farmers plan.

quests.instruction: The forecast says cloud cover will be 20% this afternoon.
quests.question: What will the sky look like?
options: Mostly clear with a few clouds
Completely covered from edge to edge
quests.correctAnswer: Mostly clear with a few clouds
quests.hint: Notice how much of the sky is covered.
quests.explanation: Only a fifth of the sky will have cloud, so most of it will be clear.
quests.funFact: Satellite pictures help measure how much of the sky is covered by cloud.

quests.instruction: A school is choosing a day for sports. Monday: 90% rain, 22°C. Tuesday: 10% rain, 27°C, light wind. Wednesday: 70% rain, strong wind. Thursday: 5% rain, 38°C, UV 11.
quests.question: Which day is best for sports?
quests.hint: A good day isn't only dry; check heat too.
quests.explanation: Tuesday is dry, mild and calm. Thursday is dry but very hot with a high UV level.
quests.funFact: Heat can matter as much as rain when planning sports.

quests.instruction: A student is asked which readings would most likely appear together on a weather report.
quests.question: Which pair fits together best?
quests.hint: Heavy rain needs a lot of cloud.
quests.explanation: Heavy rain comes from thick clouds that cover the sky. A clear sky wouldn't produce it.
quests.funFact: Heavy rain comes mostly from thick clouds that cover wide areas.

quests.instruction: A forecast symbol shows a Sun, a cloud and raindrops together.
quests.question: Which forecast does it match?
quests.hint: Count how many weather types are in the picture.
quests.explanation: Sun, cloud and raindrops together show the weather changing from bright to showery.
quests.funFact: Mixed symbols are common in spring and autumn.
